paper.title: Polyatomic ab Initio Complex Potential Energy Surfaces: Illustration of Ultracold Collisions
paper.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

research.objective: Calculate ab initio complex potential energy surfaces (CPES) for the He(2^3S) + H2 collision system using the resonances via Padé (RVP) method, and compute first-principles reaction rates for ortho- and para-H2 to interpret ultracold Penning ionization experiments.
research.system: He(2^3S, 1s2s) + H2 (rigid rotor, r0 = 0.74085 Å) → [He*–H2]* (Feshbach resonance) → He(1^1S) + H2+ + e-
key_findings: Real and imaginary parts of CPES calculated concurrently at high level (EOM-SF-CCSD(dT)/5ZP+diffuse).
Shallow potential well depths: T-shape 2.87×10^-5 hartree (6.3 cm^-1), linear 5.012×10^-5 hartree (11 cm^-1).
Decay rate Γ(R,φ) fits single exponential, confirming Penning ionization mechanism.
First-principles reaction rates (no fitting parameters) agree remarkably with sub-Kelvin experimental data for both ortho- and para-H2.
Method is general for polyatomic resonance states and large decay rates (e.g., ICD).

resonance.coordinates: Jacobi: R (He to H2 center-of-mass distance), φ (angle between R and H2 bond)

quantum_numbers.Ω: total angular momentum projection (not explicitly used)

theory.method: Resonances via Padé (RVP): stabilization technique + analytical continuation via Padé approximant

electronic_structure.method: EOM-SF-CCSD(dT) (equation-of-motion spin-flip coupled cluster with singles, doubles, perturbative triples)
electronic_structure.basis_set: Primitive 5ZP augmented with 3s,3p diffuse functions on H and 6s,6p on He (even-tempered, spacing 2.0), tight g-functions removed
electronic_structure.reference: He–H2 1^1S ground state for neutral; He–H2+ 4^S high-spin for cation

cpes_representation.expansion: V(R,φ) = Σ_j [V_j(R) - i/2 Γ_j(R)] P_j(cos φ), with V_1 = 0 by symmetry

theory.scattering_theory: Adiabatic variational theory (refs 49,50); reaction rate k(E_col) = (v_col/k_col^2) P(E_col) with transition probability P(E_col) = ∫ Ψ_f^* Γ Ψ_i dR dφ

numerical.basis_set_details: 5ZP + diffuse (3s3p on H, 6s6p on He), even-tempered spacing 2.0, tight g-functions removed, BSSE tested
numerical.convergence: Convergence with respect to diffuse functions and cardinal number ζ detailed in Supporting Information (Tables S1, S2)
numerical.geometries: φ = 0 (linear) and φ = π/2 (T-shape); R varied over wide range
numerical.decay_rate_fit: Single exponential in R (linear in log scale)

results.cpes_accuracy: Real part of CPES well approximated by bound-state EOM-SF-CCSD(dT) calculation; overlap of real eigenvalues after analytic continuation with bound-state curve.
results.penning_ionization_confirmation: Decay rate Γ(R) fits single exponential, consistent with Penning ionization model (ref 63).

reaction_rates.para_H2: Theoretical (red) and experimental (blue) curves in excellent agreement across sub-Kelvin energies (Figure 5a).
reaction_rates.no_fitting_parameters: Only fundamental constants (ħ, charges, masses) used.

results.method_universality: Demonstrates robustness for polyatomic CPES and reaction rates, applicable to large decay rates (e.g., ICD).

figures.Figure 1: Schematic representation of He*–H2 supermolecule (Jacobi coordinates R, φ, r0).
figures.Figure 2: Real potential energy curves for T-shape (φ=π/2): neutral-excited (blue) and cationic (green) states; inset shows shallow well at ~6 Å; red arrows indicate decay rate intensity.
figures.Figure 3: (a) Stabilization graph at R=1.5 Å, T-shape: eigenvalues vs real scaling parameter α; blue region = Padé input; magenta = analytically dilated curve. (b) α- and θ-trajectories showing cusp (purple arrow) at resonance.
figures.Figure 4: Ab initio CPES for T-shape: (a) Real part Re[E(R)] with inset zoom; (b) Decay rate Γ(R) with log-scale inset showing exponential fit; (c) Real parts of V_0(R) and V_2(R); (d) Decay rate components Γ_0(R) and Γ_2(R).
figures.Figure 5: Reaction rates vs collision energy: (a) para-H2 (j=0), (b) ortho-H2 (j=1). Blue = experiment (ref 48), red = theory (this work).
figures.Supporting_Information: Figure S1: Real PES for linear geometry. Figure S2: CPES for linear geometry. Tables S1, S2: Convergence tests.

equations.Eq2: E(η) = P(η)/Q(η) (Padé approximant, η = real scaling parameter)
equations.Eq3: ∂E/∂α = 0, ∂E/∂θ = 0 (stationary point conditions for η = α e^{iθ})
equations.Eq4: V(R,φ) = Σ_j [V_j(R) - i/2 Γ_j(R)] P_j(cos φ) (Legendre expansion, V_1=0)
equations.Eq6: k(E_col) = (v_col/k_col^2) P(E_col) with P(E_col) = ∫ Ψ_f^* Γ Ψ_i dR dφ

approximations: Rigid rotor approximation for H2 (fixed r0 = 0.74085 Å).
Only two geometries (φ=0, π/2) used to extract V_0 and V_2; higher Legendre terms neglected.
RVP method requires careful selection of stabilization graph data points; stability checked but not fully automated.
Basis set, while large, is finite; BSSE tested but not fully eliminated.
Adiabatic variational theory for scattering may have limitations at higher energies.
previous_work_limitations_addressed: Real and imaginary parts calculated concurrently (not separately).
No empirical fitting of imaginary part (unlike Tang-Toennies model).
No shifting of correlation energy (unlike 0.4% shift in ref 48).
Reaction rates from full complex S-matrix, not real phase-shift approximation.
